summary: Platform work every collection needs: finish and harden async template opening plus app responsiveness, CAD stones counted as stones, the hide painter in core with spikes, stamps v2, and batch 14 leftovers; each lane reviewed adversarially and fixed, then merged and verified

open: should-fix | crates/ringdesign-gui/src/app.rs:2027,2040,2054 | Defect: the worker keeps evaluating a driven graph against a `base` library that is missing the design's own artwork. For a landed template, `base` is `seed.base`. For fresh artwork, it is whatever library the last evaluation ran against. Line 2054 carries `against` forward, so `base` never catches up to the host's baked library. Any node that looks up the design's artwork by name never finds it. Master evaluated against the host's baked library from the second build on. Scenario: I built a scratch probe against this worktree that repeats the worker's calls (`evaluate_design_onto(ev, g, reg, base, host)`) on the posy graph from nodes/alpha.rs, with alpha.text "Motto" feeding alpha.library("Motto") and then layer.tiling.fit. On the branch, builds 1-4 all fail with `no alpha named "Motto"` and the tiling falls back to "Milgrain". On master, build 2 has no notes and the tiling reads "Motto". With alpha.text wired straight into layer.tiling.fit, the branch repeats `no alpha named "Motto" in the library now` on every build, so the node keeps its error rim; master clears it from build 2. In the app: open Nocturne from the menu, then add a Library alpha node for "Palmette" — it never resolves. Fix: evaluate against `job.lib`, keyed by `job.lib.revision()`. Only the nodes that read the library then re-run, once after each bake, and the shared bakes keep that cheap. Alternatively, reset `base` to the host's library once the host holds the bake.

should-fix | crates/ringdesign-gui/src/app.rs:1795,1799 (read at ui_tests.rs:342 and :604) | Defect: two new pins read the process-wide counters `GRAPH_EVALUATIONS` and `GRAPH_READS` across a multi-second wait. Any other test's app or worker that runs in the meantime moves them. CI runs `cargo test --workspace --locked` and `cargo test -p ringdesign-gui --locked` with default parallel threads. Scenario: `cargo test -p ringdesign-gui -- template graph driven --test-threads=6` failed on two runs in a row. `a_template_opens_while_the_old_design_stays_live_and_its_first_build_takes_the_open_evaluation` failed with left 6, right 5 ("the first build evaluated nothing again"). `a_driven_design_file_lands_with_its_graph_read_on_the_opening_thread` failed with left 9, right 8. The whole suite passes only with `--test-threads=1`. Fix: give each app or worker its own counters (as `DetailProbe` already does), or count on the harness's own app.

should-fix | crates/ringdesigner-android/src/app.rs:3217 | Defect: the phone's `poll_template` now handles both kinds of landing in one `Polled::Landed` branch, and it calls `editor.arrange` unconditionally. So Files > Open now re-arranges the opened file's graph. Before this branch, a phone file open ran only `GraphState::sync`, which calls `arrange_if_tangled` and leaves a tidy saved layout alone. Scenario: on the phone, move nodes in a driven design's graph, Save, then Files > Open that file. The graph shows the auto-arranged positions, and the next graph edit writes them into `design.graph` via `GraphState::changed`, so the autosave or Save loses the user's layout. Fix: arrange only for `Lands::Template`.

should-fix (integration handoff; the files are outside this lane) | crates/ringdesign-gui/src/app.rs:1046, panels/report.rs:47, panels/layers.rs:397 | Defect: deliverable 4 is not met at e7ed75f. `detail_findings()` ships as `expect(dead_code)`, and the Report and Layers panels still call `findings_in` on the UI thread every frame. Numbers from the branch's own ignored `ui_thread_costs_on_heavy_designs` test, which I ran in release on e7ed75f:

  - slowest frame while opening, landing and building: Nocturne 148.2 ms, Caiman 81.8 ms

Also, `open_measured`/`open_file(..,true,..)` add a cold measure to every open before it lands: Nocturne 1212 ms, Thalassa 1874, Vesper 5010. Fix: land the handoff with this branch. Panels read `app.detail_findings()`; `open_measured` becomes `open` and `open_file` takes `false`; delete the `expect`. Otherwise the worker's detail machinery is dead weight and the app still runs at about 13 fps on Nocturne.

should-fix — crates/ringdesign-core/src/setstone.rs:787-798 (carried, Transform arm) and :235 (held_by). Defect: when a Transform wraps a head rather than a stone, the head's stone is carried to the moved position, but the stone part stays where it was. One head then counts as two stones, and both are reported as held. The doctrine says the opposite: 'A Transform wrapped round a head would leave the stone where it was.' Failing scenario, measured with a scratch crate against 4bb2977: claw solitaire on the Court band plus Transform #9 {source: 3 (the head), translation [0,0,0.8]}. Results: set_stones = 2 and set_stones_built = 2; stones::report gives '2 stones 2.08 ct' with two lines, both made=Some("Four-claw head") and no warnings; gems::built_vertices draws 1536 triangles (two stones). The build has one stone part (#2) and an empty moved head (#9). Fix: in the Transform arm, follow the source only when is_stone(doc, source), so a moved head carries nothing. held_by/head_on should also ignore a head that a Transform consumed, so stone #2 is reported unheld. Pin: the transformed-head solitaire records 1 stone, with the 'no setting holds this stone' warning.

should-fix — crates/ringdesign-core/src/gems.rs:52 (built_vertices, `own`) together with cad/pattern.rs:619. Defect: `own` takes the first reference component whose made.gem has the same cut and size. This branch now gives a Pattern component a gem, and a pattern's mesh holds every copy in world space under an identity frame. When that pattern is the first match, every recorded stone is drawn as the whole pattern moved by the stone's frame. Failing scenario, measured: claw solitaire, Pattern #5 of stone #2 (Ring 3, builders::component(STONE)), then Transform #6 of stone #2 appended after it. #6 consumes #2, which leaves #5 as the first reference with that gem. set_stones and set_stones_built both give a correct 3 stones. But built_vertices emits 4608 triangles (6 stone bodies for 3 stones), and the farthest drawn vertex is 14.98 mm from any recorded girdle centre, so stones float off the ring. The same happens in render::finished, which feeds thumbnails and hero shots, and in both viewports once app-stones.patch lands. Fix: accept only a component whose feature is a single stone (made.key == builders::STONE, or the is_stone rule, which covers a Transform of a stone); otherwise draw the faceted stone. Pin: this design's soup has 3 stones' worth of triangles, each centred on its girdle, like the existing arrayed-claws check.

should-fix (integration) — several deliverables exist only in the unapplied scratch patches, not on 4bb2977. (a) Operation::Pattern still has `source: Id`. pattern::Sources and build_sources are unused by any Operation. The 'two-source pattern round-trips' pin exercises a test-only `Carried` struct, not Operation, and the format-6 and graph-v2 fences exist only in multi-source-pattern.patch. (b) The desktop and phone viewports still draw only reference-part meshes, in GEM_TINT. A ring array of claw heads therefore shows two empty heads while the report, sheet and stone map count 3 stones, and a tinted CAD stone is GEM_TINT in the viewport but its own tint in render::finished (deliverables 1 'gem preview' and 2 'preview and renderer agree'). The worker, sheet and stone-map exports also use the analytic record instead of report_built. Both patches pass `git apply --check` against HEAD, alone and in either order (verified without applying). The integrator must apply both, and should fix the gems.rs finding above first, because app-stones.patch routes the viewports through built_vertices.

should-fix — crates/ringdesign-core/src/setting.rs:1693-1707 (stamp_row, mirrored reflections). A reflection is dropped only when it lands in the row's own span or meets its OWN original (`plans_meet(s, .., &m, ..)`). It is never tested against the other originals or against reflections already kept, so round 1's duplicate fix is incomplete for a row whose span crosses the head unevenly. Probe on crest_band (LowDome 7x2.4), plain keel(1.2, 0.6, 0.12), PartingLine, mirror_shoulders:
  - 60..104 x4 strikes 104.00° ('right 1') and 105.33° ('right 2'): centres 0.26 mm apart, 1.2 mm keels, near-coincident.
  - 86..130 x5 strikes 83.00° ('left 2') beside 86.00° ('left 1'), 0.58 mm apart.
  - Both build with stamped 6 and 9 respectively and no notes: the doubled metal is silent.
  - The pin a_mirrored_row_across_the_head_strikes_each_station_once only tries symmetric spans (60..120, 90..118, 92..150), so it passes.
  Fix: test each reflection with plans_meet (after a may_touch cull) against every stamp already in `out`, originals and accepted reflections, not only its own original. Add a pin using 60..104 x4 or 86..130 x5.

should-fix — crates/ringdesign-core/src/dfm.rs:427 (tiered_stamps_are_judged_at_the_cost_of_their_frames). The wall-clock bound fails the core suite most of the time. Of four full runs with the documented guard (`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G --quiet -- cargo test --offline -p ringdesign-core --lib`), three failed:
  - 'Heart signet: 281.65 ms tiered against 1.19 ms on one tier'
  - 'Heart signet: 1032.77 ms tiered against 4.35 ms'
  - a third run with the same panic
  The test passes when run alone, which is how the report's '697 passed' was likely obtained. Cause:
  - The 'first' measure salts the profile width, so findings() -> field_context() -> station_tables() goes through lib.rs stretch_cached.
  - That cache is process-wide, keeps 8 entries and holds its Mutex while it builds a 360-section table.
  - Parallel tests evict its entries and serialize on that lock, so the timing measures lock waits and table builds, not the cost of stamp frames.
  Fix: assert a deterministic proxy (how many sections or kept points are computed on first sight and when judged again), or #[ignore] the test as a benchmark. Wall-clock ratios should not gate the suite.

should-fix | crates/ringdesign-core/src/parts.rs:664-676 (graph_cuts_apart) | The graph fence counts a Band `cad.feature` node wherever it stands in the node list, whether or not it lies on the chain that feeds the graph's output. The report says a band counts only when certain, and a band that feeds nothing is not certain. | Failing scenario, reproduced by a probe compiled against the branch's core rlib: take a graph from `from_document(band + Block(Separate) + Pocket(Cut))`, then rewire `source -> Block` so the Procedural shank node is left dangling. Its design input stays wired and its output feeds nothing. The evaluator builds [Block, Pocket] with no band, so the result is a ring of parts alone carrying a cut, and `cuts_apart` is true on the evaluated design. `cuts_apart_json` still returns false (probe: `band on the chain: fenced=false`, `band dangling off the chain: fenced=false`, `band deleted: fenced=true`). `graph_to_string` therefore writes the .graph.json, .cluster.json or preset at graph format 1, and desktop 0.6.0 (GRAPH_FORMAT_VERSION 1, confirmed at tag desktop-v0.6.0) opens it and pours the cutter as metal. This is the failure the fence exists to stop. Design files are safe because `in_document` reads the evaluated cad. | Fix: count a band only if it is upstream of the design the graph outputs. Walk `wires` backward from the output node, or from the nodes behind a cluster's exposed `outputs`. With no output to walk from, treat every band as uncertain. Pin the dangling-band case in both the graph and the cluster JSON tables, and in the graph-crate evaluation test (`apart(g) == true`, version 2).

result.integration:
Batch 15 is integrated on master at `9992ffa`, not pushed. Every suite and all four checks are green. The live checks turned up two bugs and I fixed both: opening Caiman deadlocked the phone, and the first Undo of a graph edit did nothing.

## Merges
All five lanes are merged with `--no-ff`, as "Merge <branch>":

| Lane | Merge commit |
|---|---|
| b15-leftovers | `58f6ad8` |
| b15-stamps | `5fd9390` |
| b15-skin | `537451a` |
| b15-cad-stones | `d3dfa34` |
| b15-open-speed | `a8e3425` |

Resolutions:
- **Merge conflict:** only `library.rs` `format_version_for`. It now checks five fences: stored mesh, in-plane revolution, pattern of several parts, cut on a ring of parts alone, and a stamp that isn't plain. The stale format-6 doc lines are rewritten.
- **Semantic conflicts:** two `Stamp` literals lacked `tier`/`top` (`parting_stamp_probe.rs` and the phone's `cad/stamp.rs` test) — `d339745`.
- **Patches the lanes left:**
  - leftovers' `phone-sketch-cut.patch` and `pick-highlight-pockets.patch` — `cb11863`.
  - cad-stones' `multi-source-pattern.patch`, applied 3-way with conflicts in `library.rs` and graph `file.rs`; both sets of fences kept — `4a99e62`.
  - cad-stones' `app-stones.patch`, applied after the `gems.rs` fix — `ccf6731`.
- **CAD thumbnails:** regenerated and committed — `7bfc7fc`.

## Reviewer should-fixes (each pin fails without its fix)
- **leftovers:** a Band node counts toward the graph fence only if it feeds the first `sink.output` (or every exposed output of a cluster); with no output, no band counts — `f758808`.
- **stamps** — `adb0c9e`:
  - A mirrored reflection is tested against every stamp already struck, not just its own original. In a row whose stations don't touch, any overlap drops it; in a crowded row, only one closer than half the pitch. Pinned at 60..104 ×4 and 86..130 ×5.
  - The wall-clock DFM pin now counts surface points made instead: 24 on first sight, 0 when judged again, and 48 without the cache.
  - Bench stamps no longer decide which frame the cast stamps are struck on (the reviewer's nit).
- **cad-stones** — `068e897`:
  - A Transform wrapped round a head carries no stone, and the moved head holds nothing: 1 stone, unheld, instead of 2, both held.
  - `built_vertices` draws a stone only from a stone part's own mesh (it drew a whole pattern at each stone).
  - The pattern fence counts `source` and `sources` together.
  - `rigid()` is replaced by `cad::rotate_place` — `e7f3c9b`.
- **open-speed** — `cfdf9f1`:
  - The worker evaluates against the host's library, so a node reading the design's own artwork by name resolves from the 2nd build.
  - Counters are per worker (evaluations) and per thread (graph reads); the formerly flaky pins pass twice at `--test-threads=6`.
  - The phone arranges only a template's graph on landing, not an opened file's (`GraphState::landed`).
  - The Report and Layers panels read `detail_findings()`; opens no longer measure detail on their own thread. The detail pin now reads through the Report panel — `6d961a7`.
- **skin nit:** the keyframed atlas is pinned within 0.005 mm of the swept mesh — `e9b64f7`.
- **Phone test update:** a ring of parts alone now offers Cut while one of its parts is metal — `30f0506`.

## Bugs found live and fixed
- **Phone deadlock opening Caiman on rdsmoke — `3c9f64e`.**
  - Symptom: the app showed "isn't responding".
  - Cause, from the native stacks: the UI thread held egui's Context lock while waiting on the rayon pool for tessellation. All four pool workers were inside the bake, calling the open's progress wake (`request_repaint`), and waiting for that same lock.
  - Fix: a progress update now only signals a dedicated `template-wake` thread, which does the wake.
  - Pin: lives in the GUI crate, because workbench builds core without `parallel`. The old code woke 5 times from pool threads.
- **The first Undo of a graph edit did nothing — `908fe59`.**
  - Symptom: History read "Graph edited", then "Profile width 14 mm -> 15 mm", and one Undo left the width at 15.
  - Fix: `History::absorb` folds the evaluated result into the edit's entry, on desktop and phone. Pinned in core and the GUI.
  - The same path exists on master, so this predates batch 15.

0 failures anywhere. The first run had two failures, both from the patches' intended behaviour changes; the test updates above fixed them.

## Checks
All four are clean:
- `cargo check --offline --workspace --all-targets`: 0 warnings.
- `cargo check --locked --offline --workspace`.
- NDK arm64 (`cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a check -p ringdesigner_android`).
- wasm (core and configurator, `--no-default-features`).

## Live checks (screenshots in `…/scratchpad/shots/`)
- **Cancel Caiman midway:** the plate read "Opening Caiman — armoured hide — reading it"; after Cancel, "Stopped opening Caiman — armoured hide: the design is unchanged". Lorica stayed on screen. `b15-caiman-opening.png`, `b15-caiman-cancelled.png`.
- **Caiman fully:** cold, it landed 0.22 s after the click and showed built at 1.18 s; warm, landing took 0.34 s. `b15-caiman-open.png`, `b15-caiman-cold-open.png`.
- **Undo/redo on Caiman:** each round trip under 0.2 s including the driver. After the fix there is one "Graph edited" entry, and one Undo restores the width. `b15-caiman-history.png` (before), `b15-caiman-history-fixed.png`, `b15-caiman-undo-fixed.png`, `b15-caiman-redo-fixed.png`.
- **Claw solitaire (CAD › Example projects):** the stone shows in the viewport. Report › Stones reads "1 stones 1.04 ct", Round 6.5 mm, edge clearance 0.53 mm, pavilion depth 4.32 mm. The stone map exported with the stone. `b15-claw-cad.png`, `b15-claw-model.png`, `b15-claw-report.png`, `b15-claw-stonemap.png` / `.svg`.
- **Phone (rdsmoke, emulator-5554, x86_64 release):** before the fix, Caiman's open hung (`b15-phone-caiman-anr.png`). After it, the plate showed "building the ring" at about 2 s with Nocturne still live, and Caiman was built by about 4 s. `b15-phone-caiman-building.png`, `b15-phone-caiman.png`, `b15-phone-caiman-sequence.png`.
- `app.ron` was backed up and is restored byte for byte; the app was closed with alt+F4.

A rebuild of an unchanged graph costs 0.1–6.3 ms across the catalogue.

**UI thread, release, ms:** "before" is e7ed75f's own binary run today at the same load. Caiman's history and save rows rise to 47–88 ms while the worker's cold detail measure is running, then settle to the values shown.

**Spikes:**
- **Sand masters, bare:**
  - Castable: 002, 006, 015, 017.
  - Marginal: 001 (0.10%), 012 (0.21%), 013 (0.066%).
  - NotCastable: 003 Clover 13.2% at −74.8°, 005 Rosette 6.6%, 007 Quatrefoil 14.7%, 016 Star 2.9%. This matters for Viscum, Sigillum, Chelonia and Phrynosoma.
- **013 to 16 mm:** possible in two resize steps. Sand comes out at 0.045% undercut at −1.1°; wax is Castable.
- **Prickle:** a hook lying in the parting plane is clean. Tilted 2° it blocks at 0.075 mm; spun 90° it blocks.
- **Side-face gate spill:** at 1.36× width and 1.00× thickness, 0.51 mm of cells spill onto the crown fillet, NotCastable 3.43%. Keys holding thickness at or above width stay clean.
- **Holly leaf on 006's parting line:** clean up to a 20° spine lean; 25° blocks. The −40° row is invalid because the stamp failed to join.

## Open
- **Open speed:**
  - The phone's first build after a landing evaluates the graph again (`ringdesigner-android/src/ring.rs:518`).
  - The worker's cold detail measure uses every core for 1.4–4.4 s after a landing and slows the UI thread meanwhile (`ringdesign-gui/src/app.rs:1982`).
  - `history::describe` costs 31 ms per commit on Caiman (`ringdesign-core/src/history.rs:274`).
- **Renders:** turntables and PNG renders on desktop, phone and configurator are metal only (`gui/src/export.rs:282`, `:302`; `android/src/export.rs:274`, `:278`; `configurator/src/main.rs:322`).
- **CAD stones:**
  - The section view records every stone every frame, 92 ms per drag frame with 24 heads (`panels/section.rs:330`).
  - `Frames::built` always returns true (`setstone.rs:721`).
  - The stone map labels a CAD family "Round 6.5 mm 6.5" (`stonemap.rs:91`).
- **Fences:**
  - A graph's `/stamps` patch and standalone graph files aren't fenced for tier/top (`graph/src/file.rs:60`).
  - The graph fence still under-reads a `flow.if` with two chains, a wired operation pin, and a root-pointer `design.set` (`parts.rs:677`).
- **Parts alone:**
  - A pocket's walls name the cut, so selecting the part misses them (`parts.rs:716`).
  - `carved_apart` swallows a failed boolean (`parts.rs:819`).
  - A partly buried seam still gets its whole bead (`parts.rs:224`).
  - The primitive's rest zone snaps back to 2 mm when a drag returns under 0.2 mm (`command/commands.rs:941`).
- **Skin:**
  - Station-aware side-face gates, P5 (`field.rs:443`).
  - The draft rule is first order (`skin.rs:408`).
  - `skin::hash` is a generic public name (`skin.rs:332`).
  - The crease census reads sliver faces (`examples/stock_spike.rs:76`).
  - The −40° csg join fails with "two cuts cross inside a face".
- **Housekeeping:**
  - Desktop saves are detached threads sharing one `.tmp` name and aren't joined on exit (`gui/src/export.rs:472`).
  - The shared bake cache holds up to 48 M texels, about 200 MB, on the phone too (`alpha.rs:686`).
  - The status line is rewritten every frame of an open (`app.rs:709`).
  - The template plate overlaps the ring view's info card (seen live).
- **Doctrine-level, unchanged:** the axial web and `LayerEntry::stage`.

## Cleanup
- All five b15 worktrees are removed and the five branches deleted, after confirming each was merged.
- The `handoff`, `bestiarium-arachne` and `bestiarium-draco` worktrees belong to other work and are untouched.
- The docs are committed in `9992ffa`: the PLAN.md Batch 15 block, and CLAUDE.md on the skin and sand master, stamps v2, CAD stones and `render::finished`, open costs, the pool/egui wake rule, `History::absorb`, and the glibc arena lesson.
- Nothing is pushed or published. rdsmoke is still running.
